question: What is the main goal of sterilization?

options.A: The removal of visible blood stains from metal surfaces
options.B: The elimination of dust and organic dirt from equipment
options.C: The complete removal or destruction of all microbial life
options.D: The reduction of harmful bacteria to safe levels on skin

explanation: Sterilization is all about getting rid of every single germ and tough spore so nothing is left alive. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is sterilization stricter and more powerful than standard disinfection?

options.A: It only applies to items that touch intact human skin
options.B: It can be completed in a few seconds using simple wipes
options.C: It targets and kills bacterial spores as well as vegetative cells
options.D: It is performed using mild soaps and warm running water

explanation: Disinfection kills a lot of germs, but tough bacterial spores can survive it. Sterilization goes the extra mile to destroy those resilient spores completely! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of these steps must you always do first before disinfecting or sterilizing equipment?
explanation: Always wash off blood, dirt, and tissue first! If dirt is left on the tool, it shields the germs from the disinfecting or sterilizing agents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: A nurse wipes down a bedside table with a chemical disinfectant. What is the expected result?

options.A: Most pathogenic germs are killed, but bacterial spores may survive
options.B: The surface becomes completely sterile for surgical procedures
options.C: All living microorganisms and tough spores are completely destroyed
options.D: Only visible dust and physical dirt are physically washed away

explanation: Disinfectants are great for cleaning surfaces and killing most harmful germs, but they don't always wipe out tough bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: You are getting instruments ready for a deep abdominal surgery. How must these tools be processed?
explanation: Any tool going into sterile body tissue or blood vessels is a critical item and absolutely must be sterilized! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: An item touches a patient's unbroken skin during a routine check-up. According to Spaulding's rules, what level of processing does it need?
explanation: Items that only touch intact skin are non-critical and just need basic low-level disinfection between patients. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: What does an autoclave mainly use to achieve full sterilization?
explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam, which packs enough heat to rapidly destroy all germs and spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why might a nurse choose dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave for certain sharp tools or powders?

options.A: Dry heat uses steam pressure to penetrate thick plastic wrappers
options.B: Dry heat takes only two minutes to complete a full cycle
options.C: Dry heat is much cheaper to operate than electricity
options.D: Dry heat does not cause rusting or damage to moisture-sensitive items

explanation: Steam can rust fine metal edges or ruin powders. Dry heat is a wonderful alternative when you need to avoid moisture! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which chemical agent requires a special airing-out (aeration) period because it leaves toxic gas behind?
explanation: Ethylene oxide is a strong sterilizing gas, but items need to sit in a special aeration chamber afterward to clear out lingering toxic fumes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a big plus of using hydrogen peroxide gas plasma compared to older gas methods?

options.A: It works instantly without needing any special packaging
options.B: It can be performed easily using standard washbasins
options.C: It operates at low temperatures and leaves no toxic residue
options.D: It is the cheapest method available for hospital wards

explanation: Gas plasma is gentle on delicate equipment and breaks down into harmless water and oxygen, skipping the long wait for aeration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which check is considered the ultimate gold standard to confirm your autoclave cycle actually worked?

options.A: Biological indicators containing resistant bacterial spores
options.B: Checking the machine door seal for visible steam leaks
options.C: Reviewing the nurse's handwritten checklist after a shift
options.D: A quick visual check of the external packaging tape color

explanation: Using actual resistant spores in biological indicators gives us the absolute best proof that the machine killed the toughest germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main drawback of relying only on a chemical indicator strip on the outside of a sterile pack?

options.A: It can tell the exact internal temperature reached deep inside the metal tray
options.B: It permanently destroys the bacterial spores hidden inside the pack
options.C: It requires a laboratory incubator to read the final color change
options.D: It only shows that the pack was exposed to heat or gas, not that it is truly sterile

explanation: Color changes on the outside just prove the pack went into the machine; they don't guarantee every single germ inside was destroyed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for packaged instruments sitting in storage?

options.A: Sterility depends entirely on the specific time of day it was processed
options.B: Instruments lose their sterility the moment they are placed on a shelf
options.C: All items automatically expire exactly seven days after autoclaving
options.D: Items remain sterile until the packaging is damaged or exposed to moisture

explanation: Instead of worrying about a strict calendar expiration date, packs stay sterile as long as the packaging remains safe and dry! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: A nurse picks up a sterile surgical tray from the supply room and notices the outer paper wrapper is damp. What should she do?

options.A: Dry the outside wrapper carefully with a clean towel and use it
options.B: Check the chemical indicator strip and use the tray if the color changed
options.C: Consider the item contaminated and return it for re-sterilization
options.D: Open the package immediately before the moisture spreads further

explanation: Moisture on packaging acts like a sponge, pulling bacteria right through the barrier. It's best to safely reprocess it! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)
